title: Bacteria in a Hot Spring? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
On a cycling trip, Aarav stops at a steaming hot spring where tiny microbes live in the hot water, and asks: are they the same kind of life as the bacteria in curd? Under a microscope they look alike, but inside they are very different.

You will see the five kingdoms and the difference between a prokaryote and a eukaryote, then a zoom ladder from a cell to a ribosome to ribosomal RNA, the molecule Carl Woese compared. Watch the comparison run step by step (read, line up, count the differences, grow the tree), meet the three domains proposed in 1990 by Woese, Kandler and Wheelis (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya), compare Bacteria with Archaea, and sort six organisms into domains. Then the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. Note: this topic is not in the current rationalised NCERT text.

This is Episode 10 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
